question: [scripted] ECHO-02: does weighing explanations against its own predictions tell the fly's own changes from outside ones better than a simpler sensorimotor rule?
hypothesis: [scripted] A motion-gated rule (a change met while moving is its own, one met standing is the world's) explains fewer hidden held-out changes correctly than the full self-model.
competing_hypothesis: [scripted] Whether the fly was moving when a change began is all the evidence there is, so the rule does as well as the self-model.
